messages:
zara: FYI hit a subtle SSE reassembly bug in the node sampleapp when a reconnect happens during a large `data:` payload. JSON.parse blows up with '\n' token.

kevin: can you share the raw chunk sequence? is this the streaming helper or the eventsource shim?

zara: streaming helper. repro with `tc qdisc` to delay packets for ~150ms. capture (trimmed):```
# chunk before drop
id: 210
data: {"t":"part1\nwith newline\"}

# resume first chunk



data: {"t":"part2"}
``` when we concat the tail+head the naive `split('\n\n')` produces an empty segment + a partial JSON fragment, then parse fails.

marta: Node Buffer pooling sometimes returns a Buffer that begins with a slice of a previous allocation; if your reassembly code trims leading newlines incorrectly you can end up with `\n` characters before the JSON starts.

frank: Quick mitigation: on resume, drop leading blank lines before handing chunks to JSON.parse, AND defensively ignore empty-events. Long term: switch to an incremental line-state parser that preserves partial lines and only emits events on an exact blank line (CRLF or LF).

kevin: also ensure we send `Last-Event-ID` on reconnects so server can avoid resending parts that would be stitched incorrectly.

zara: I prototyped a tiny fix: replace `buffer.split('\n\n')` with a line-oriented loop that keeps `partialLine` across chunks and emits events only when a full blank line seen. Put a `--sse-raw` flag to dump raw frames in CI.

marta: good. add a non-flaky netem integration test that drops in the middle of a `data:` line and asserts no parse exceptions. Also add a parity test entry so browser/node/python runs the same scenario.

ci-bot: created issue #4389: "sse: node sampleapp incremental parser + netem parity test" and queued CI for branch zara/sse-buffer-pool-reassembly-fix.

kevin: when you open the PR, include the failing raw capture and a short note about buffer pooling causing leading newline bytes — that'll help reviewers.

zara: will do. opening PR with incremental parser, `--sse-raw` toggle, netem test, and the capture. will ping for review. :rocket:
